extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and panel members for UKRI (BBSRC and EPSRC) grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing and assessing research grant proposals submitted to UKRI councils BBSRC and EPSRC, including scoring, procedural steps, and the specific assessment criteria each council uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal UKRI Scoring (1-6 Scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Six-point adjectival/numerical scale used across UKRI: 6 - Exceptional; 5 - Excellent; 4 - Good; 3 - Fair; 2 - Weak; 1 - Poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 6 = outstanding, addresses all criteria at exceptional level; 5 = very high quality, very minor weaknesses; 4 = addresses criteria well with some weaknesses; 3 = some merit but significant weaknesses; 2 = flaws that prevent funding; 1 = unsuitable for funding. Used to translate reviewer judgements into panel scoring and ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBSRC review process (procedural steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: BBSRC proposals are considered by three or more peer reviewers, applicants may provide a PI response, then proposals, reviews and PI responses are considered by an assessment panel which produces a rank-ordered list; panel recommendations are considered internally by BBSRC leading to final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process steps imply reviewers should provide independent, evidence-based reviews suitable for panel synthesis; reviewers should be aware that panels moderate rather than re-review and will use reviewers' comments plus PI responses to prioritise funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance / significance of the research (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the importance or significance of the research being proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider scientific and societal importance, potential to advance the field, and relevance to BBSRC's remit and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the research proposal (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the overall quality of the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of aims, robustness of hypotheses, appropriateness of methodology and experimental design, feasibility, and coherence across workpackages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of investigators (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the past performance and suitability of the investigators proposing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publications, prior funding, relevant expertise, and evidence of the team’s ability to deliver the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the suitability of the host institution(s) and research environment for delivering the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, facilities, collaborations, and whether the environment adds credibility or unique capability to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic alignment with BBSRC priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how well the proposal aligns with BBSRC strategic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the proposal supports council objectives and priorities and how strongly it aligns with strategic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value for money (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the project represents good value for the requested funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cost-effectiveness, justification of requested resources, and whether expected outputs justify budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and responsible research and innovation considerations (BBSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ethical implications and responsible research practices related to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ethical approvals required, RRI issues, data management, and broader impacts or risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPSRC review process (procedural steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSRC applications are reviewed independently by at least three peers, assessed against published criteria, and if sufficiently supported go to a prioritisation panel which scores and ranks them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should produce independent assessments addressing published areas of assessment; panels act to synthesise those reviews rather than re-review applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (EPSRC) — importance, originality, ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the intrinsic quality of the proposal, including importance, originality and ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work is scientifically rigorous, novel, and ambitious in scope or potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and timeliness (EPSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the importance of the research question and its timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the topic addresses a current, significant need or opportunity and whether timing affects potential impact or relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant capability (EPSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the capability of the applicants to deliver the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider track record, expertise, team composition, and evidence of capacity to complete the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and management (EPSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the adequacy of the resources requested and the proposed project management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess justification of staff, equipment, consumables, and whether management plans and milestones are realistic and adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: National importance (EPSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the importance of the proposal to national priorities or needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alignment with national strategic priorities, potential benefits to the UK, and breadth of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations (EPSRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ethical issues arising from the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider required approvals, potential harm, responsible practice and any mitigating measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel function: moderation and synthesis (UKRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment panels act as moderating panels and do not re-review proposals; they synthesise peer reviews and rank proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide clear, evidence-based comments because panels will moderate using those reviews and the PI response to prioritise applications rather than redoing detailed assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles of Assessment; prioritise excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should weigh scientific excellence in their judgements and justify excellence-related scores with evidence from the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; consider diversity in assessment and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply diversity-aware practices in reviewer selection and assessment; be mindful of inclusive evaluation and potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; consider alignment with organisational mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how proposals contribute to the missions of the council and UKRI more broadly when making funding priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Trust
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; maintain trust in the assessment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act with integrity, confidentiality and professionalism; provide fair, evidence-based reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; ensure transparent assessment and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reasons for evaluations, avoid unexplained or opaque judgements, and follow published processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; ensure impartial and unbiased decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare and manage conflicts of interest; evaluate proposals on merits without undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; conduct assessments efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely, focused reviews and make efficient use of panel time and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: UKRI principle: Continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: One of UKRI's Eight Core Principles; seek to improve assessment processes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive feedback on the process and adopt best practices to improve future assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Three or more peer reviewers are used per proposal across UKRI councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect that their independent assessment will be one of at least three inputs synthesised by panels; produce standalone, defensible reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI response opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are given an opportunity to provide a PI response to peer reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should make clear, substantive points and identify key issues because applicants will have a chance to respond; panels will consider reviews and PI responses together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjectival/numerical scoring is used
rubrics_metrics.description: UKRI uses adjectival and numerical scoring (e.g., the 1–6 scale) to record reviewer judgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should map qualitative judgements to the 1–6 scale consistently and justify scores in their commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic alignment considered (common across councils)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic alignment with council priorities is considered during assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note and comment on how well the proposal aligns with strategic aims where relevant; strategic fit can influence prioritisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, diversity and inclusion policies applied
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) policies are applied in review and decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should be aware of and apply EDI policies, avoid biased language or judgements, and consider equitable practices in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of generative AI by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not permitted to use generative AI for assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessment content should be produced without relying on generative AI tools; adhere to council guidance on acceptable tools and methods.
